issueCommentThread.body: Hold (2026-09-18 eval of 4749-4765 vs current WIP and Unreleased/0.119.3). UAT was on 0.119.1. v0.119.3 #4718 recut Doctor Next command. Remaining help copy (one next step) vs Resolution: proceed is polish, not a current blocker versus in-progress #4723.

Adoption blocker.

This is about Lifecycle: installing Directive, updating it, and getting one clear next step when something looks wrong. It also covers whether the version someone thinks they installed is the version that is actually running.

What a new person hits: The help text says the doctor command will print the one next step. In practice it says "proceed," which is not a command, and the warning lists two different commands.

Why that ruins the product for them: The command they run when they are lost does not tell them what to do. Two testers, on different machines, stopped on this.

How likely: High. Doctor is the advertised way to find out what to do next, so people run it on the first day.

Re-measured at dispatch SHA `ef4f29f5ab595faf26a3b00194d3dbdc9f97a085`:

- `packages/core/src/doctor/help.ts` still says "Diagnose the Directive install and print the one next step."
- `packages/cli/src/dispatch.ts` doctor summary uses the same phrase.
- `runResolutionDecision` prints `Resolution: proceed -- ${rootCauseLine}.` when `plan.mode` is proceed (no `Next command:` line).
- `checkCanonicalVendoredNpmSignpost` fail detail still concatenates `CANONICAL_UPGRADE_COMMAND` (`npm i -g @deftai/directive@latest`) then `directive migrate`.

#4718 recut Next command (align-pin). #4723 recut missing-core clean skip. #4767 closed as duplicate of this number. Those lands do not rewrite help.ts or collapse the two-command signpost.

What this P1 is not:

- Not the dirty UNRESOLVED versus --full proceed split (#4886 / #4701).
- Not README --full omission (#4673).

## 1. The P1 is unlabeled advisory copy on a matching-pin proceed `sharpens-framing`

Evidence: `plan()` already returns mode `proceed` with `command: null` and root cause `engine ${effectiveEngine} matches pin ${facts.pinVersion} and content is current` (`packages/core/src/resolution/plan.ts`). `runResolutionDecision` prints `Resolution: proceed -- ${rootCauseLine}.` and emits `Next command:` only when `actionRequired` (`plan.mode !== "proceed"`). That proceed branch is tested (`healthy deposit + legacy vbrief -> proceed; secondary migrate advice only after primary clears`; `countNextCommands === 0`). `checkCanonicalVendoredNpmSignpost` is in `DOCTOR_ADVISORY_FAIL_CHECKS`, `stampAdvisory`s the fail, and `runInstallIntegrityChecks` maps it to `severity: "warning"` so `errorCount` / `lastErrorCount` stay 0. Warning-only footer is `System check completed with ${warningCount} warning(s).` (exit 0). Help still says "Diagnose the Directive install and print the one next step." (`help.ts`); CLI summary is the same phrase (`dispatch.ts`). The signpost fail detail concatenates `` `CANONICAL_UPGRADE_COMMAND` `` (`npm i -g @deftai/directive@latest`) then `` `directive migrate` ``. Throttle-skip already labels the same class of findings `Signpost advisory: N local configuration / layout note(s)`. Full probe prints the raw detail as a generic warning. Init writes VERSION without `managedBy` (`init-deposit.ts` `manifestFields`), then `printMigrateNudgeIfNeeded` emits `MIGRATE_COMPLETION_NUDGE` (one command, provenance, idempotent). Session-start uses the same nudge. That is the UAT path: init, then doctor, matching pin, one advisory, two verbs in the warning.

Failure mode: A first-day consumer is promised one next step, sees `proceed` (not a command), and reads two upgrade verbs in a warning that still exits 0. Two UAT testers stopped on that screen.

Disposition: Bind as fork (c) plus the two help strings. Full-probe footer reuses the throttle `Signpost advisory:` label so the warning cannot be read as the next step. Signpost detail reuses `MIGRATE_COMPLETION_NUDGE` (`directive migrate` only). Help and CLI summary follow the existing resolution contract: one `Next command:` when `actionRequired`, else `Resolution: proceed`. `System check passed!` remains the zero-warning footer.

## 2. Fork (b) on this path copies an upgrade recipe `sharpens-framing`

Evidence: `directive migrate` is a thin provenance stamp: on-disk shape unchanged, never downloads (`init-deposit/migrate.ts`). `CANONICAL_UPGRADE_COMMAND` is the post-freeze global upgrade (`doctor/constants.ts`). `VENDORED_NPM_DEPOSIT_UPGRADE_COMMAND` (`${CANONICAL_UPGRADE_COMMAND} && deft update`) is the stale-payload suggestion in `payload-staleness.ts`, a different row. The signpost inlines the upgrade recipe onto a matching-pin install. `plan()` already chose proceed with `command: null`. Secondary migrate advice already prints as `note:` after proceed.

Failure mode: A Bound-remedy that lifts the current signpost pair, or `@latest` alone, into `Next command:` upgrades a pin-matched engine. The next doctor run is then skew / `align-pin` (#4718), a new problem the tester did not have.

Disposition: If synthesis keeps a documented-re-run fork, the command is `directive migrate`, kept as advisory/`note:` (same pattern as proceed + `migrate:xbrief`). `plan.mode` stays `proceed`. The check stays in `DOCTOR_ADVISORY_FAIL_CHECKS`.

## 3. The three open forks already have homes `sharpens-framing`

Inventory at this SHA: `runResolutionDecision` (exactly one primary `Next command:`); `plan.warnings` as `note:`; `isDoctorAdvisoryFail` / `DOCTOR_ADVISORY_FAIL_CHECKS` / `stampAdvisory`; throttle `Signpost advisory:`; `System check passed!` when `warningCount === 0`; `MIGRATE_COMPLETION_NUDGE` / `shouldEmitMigrateNudge` / `printMigrateNudgeIfNeeded` on init, update, and session-start.

Failure mode: A new `healthy` `plan.mode`, a fourth next-action surface, or stamping `managed_by` at init would recut the classifier, the #3379 advisory-fail set, or the #2059 one-time migrate verb. Stop 1 already excluded a new migrate verb.

Disposition: Map fork (a) onto `Resolution: proceed` plus `System check passed!` / labeled advisories. Map fork (b) onto `MIGRATE_COMPLETION_NUDGE` as a labeled note. Map fork (c) onto the throttle advisory label extended to the full probe. Reuse those; do not add a parallel doctor contract.

## Road not taken

A new `healthy` resolution token. Steelman: testers wanted a done verdict. Flip: the Bound-remedy needs a word other than proceed and `System check passed!`. Those two already exist; advisory labeling is what unblocks the passed footer.

Promoting `directive migrate` to primary `Next command:`. Steelman: it is runnable and re-verifiable (signpost skips after stamp). Flip: unstamped provenance must fail-close first-day doctor. That recuts #3379 and the proceed + secondary-note test. The stamped P1 is the advertised copy contract.

## Footnotes `footnote`

- Injection / swarm lens does not fire: this recut is doctor help and advisory copy.
- #4718 remains the align-pin Next-command row (engine ahead, content at engine). It does not rewrite `help.ts` or the signpost detail.
- `signpost-checks.test.ts` asserts the check name only. The two-command fail detail is unpinned.

metadata.issueBody:
**Tester 3 · focused-test-pass-1**

## Summary
`directive doctor`'s help text says it will "print the one next step." In practice a run can exit 0 with 1 warning where the single-next-action block says `proceed` (not a command) and the warning body enumerates **two** commands (`npm i -g @deftai/directive@latest`, then `directive migrate`). Neither arm of the contract is satisfied.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Install Directive: `npm i -g @deftai/directive`.
2. `directive init` in a fresh project.
3. Run:
   ```
   directive doctor
   ```

## Expected
Either doctor reports "healthy" clearly, or it prints exactly one actionable next command that can be run and re-verified.

## Actual
- Exit 0, 0 errors, 1 warning (`canonical-vendored-npm-signpost`).
- Closing line: `System check completed with 1 warning(s).`
- Resolution block: `✓ Resolution: proceed -- engine 0.119.1 matches pin 0.119.1 and content is current.`
- Warning body lists two commands: `npm i -g @deftai/directive@latest`, then `directive migrate`.

Because "proceed" isn't a command, users can't verify the fix. Because there are two commands in the warning, "one next step" is inaccurate.

## Suggested fix
Collapse this to one of: (a) a genuine `healthy` verdict, (b) a single actionable command with a documented re-run, or (c) a labeled advisory that explicitly is not a "next step."

## Environment
- Directive: `@deftai/directive-core@0.119.1`
- OS: macOS

## Also reported

#4767 (UAT Tester 4, Windows, 0.119.2 and again after upgrade to 0.119.3) is the same doctor contract break: exit 0, no single next command, canonical-vendored warning. Closed as a duplicate of this Tester 3 report. Two testers move this from Medium to High.
